acceptance: `evolve loop --resume --cycle N` with two live checkpoints resumes N, not the newer one (red: flag provided but not defined)
--cycle naming a cycle without a checkpoint exits 1 and lists the live checkpoints
--from-phase after the checkpointed phase, or outside the cycle's plan, exits 10
fix: Add `--cycle N` and `--from-phase P` to `evolve loop --resume`. --cycle restricts discovery to cycle N's checkpoint through a ResumeOptions filter, so discovery stays one function; when N has no checkpoint it exits 1 listing the live ones. --from-phase restarts RunCycleFromPhase at P when P is at or before the checkpointed phase in that cycle's plan; a phase outside the plan or after the checkpoint exits 10. Either flag without --resume exits 10. Document both flags in runtime-reference.md's operator commands.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: `evolve loop --resume` calls core.LoadResumeState with empty ResumeOptions (cmd_loop_resume.go:25), and discovery takes the newest resumable per-run checkpoint (core/resume.go:79, discoverPerRunResumeState). No flag names a cycle or a phase. On 2026-09-28 a signal-stopped fleet wave resumed cycle 1709's day-old checkpoint instead of its stopped lanes (inbox resume-after-a-fleet-signal-stop). Resuming a specific cycle, or restarting one from an earlier phase, takes `evolve cycle reset` and a fresh launch, which throws the checkpoint away.
title: `evolve loop --resume` always takes the newest checkpoint; add `--cycle N` and `--from-phase P` so the operator resumes the cycle they mean
